instruction: How do I list all running processes on the system?
output:
Command: ps aux
Meaning: Shows every running process with username, PID, CPU and memory utilization.

instruction: How do I monitor active processes in real time?
output:
Command: top
Meaning: Displays an updating real-time list of system processes and resource usage. Press q to exit.

instruction: How do I launch an enhanced interactive process monitor?
output:
Command: htop
Meaning: Provides a colored, scrollable, interactive overview of CPU cores, RAM, and processes.

instruction: How do I kill a process gracefully using its PID?
output:
Command: kill <PID>
Meaning: Sends SIGTERM (15) to request the process to clean up and exit safely.

instruction: How do I force kill a stubborn or frozen process?
output:
Command: kill -9 <PID>
Meaning: Sends SIGKILL (9) terminating the process immediately without cleanup.
Warning: Unsaved work is lost. Use only if a standard kill fails.

instruction: How do I kill processes matching a program name?
output:
Command: pkill <process_name>
Meaning: Terminates all running processes whose names match the given pattern.
Warning: Check the name carefully as it terminates all matching instances.

instruction: How do I kill all instances of a program by exact name?
output:
Command: killall -9 <name>
Meaning: Sends SIGKILL to every process whose name exactly matches the argument.
Warning: Terminates all instances unconditionally.

instruction: How do I run a command in the background?
output:
Command: python script.py &
Meaning: Appending & releases the terminal prompt immediately while the job runs in the background.

instruction: How do I see active background jobs in the current shell?
output:
Command: jobs -l
Meaning: Lists background tasks started from the current shell along with their job IDs and PIDs.

instruction: How do I bring background job 1 back to the foreground?
output:
Command: fg %1
Meaning: Transfers job number 1 from the background into active terminal interaction.

instruction: How do I continue a suspended job in the background?
output:
Command: bg %1
Meaning: Resumes execution of stopped job number 1 without tying up the terminal.

instruction: How do I run a long task that persists after logging out?
output:
Command: nohup ./long_job.sh &
Meaning: Runs the command immune to SIGHUP hangups, writing output to nohup.out.

instruction: How do I start a CPU-intensive script with lower priority?
output:
Command: nice -n 10 ./task.sh
Meaning: Starts the process with a nice value of 10, yielding CPU time to other tasks.

instruction: How do I launch a program with highest scheduling priority?
output:
Command: sudo nice -n -20 ./realtime.sh
Meaning: Starts the process with highest CPU priority.
Warning: Requires root privileges.

instruction: How do I adjust the priority of an already running process?
output:
Command: renice +5 -p 1234
Meaning: Changes the scheduling priority of PID 1234 to nice value +5.

instruction: How do I find the process ID of a running program?
output:
Command: pidof nginx
Meaning: Returns the process ID for the specified executable name.

instruction: How do I search for a PID using a keyword?
output:
Command: pgrep -l python
Meaning: Searches running processes and prints the PID and command name matching 'python'.

instruction: How do I view the full process hierarchy as a tree?
output:
Command: pstree -p
Meaning: Draws a tree diagram of processes showing parent-child relationships and PIDs.

instruction: How do I trace system calls executed by a binary?
output:
Command: strace -c ./program
Meaning: Intercepts and counts kernel system calls made during program execution.

instruction: How do I trace shared library calls in a binary?
output:
Command: ltrace ./program
Meaning: Intercepts dynamic library calls made by the executable.

instruction: How do I check CPU affinity of a process?
output:
Command: taskset -p 1234
Meaning: Shows which CPU cores process 1234 is allowed to run on.

instruction: How do I bind a process to run only on core 0?
output:
Command: taskset -c 0 ./program
Meaning: Restricts program execution strictly to CPU core 0.

instruction: How do I check system uptime and load average?
output:
Command: uptime
Meaning: Displays how long the system has been up, user count, and load averages over 1, 5, and 15 mins.

instruction: How do I inspect virtual memory and CPU statistics periodically?
output:
Command: vmstat 2 5
Meaning: Reports memory, paging, I/O blocks, and CPU activity every 2 seconds for 5 reports.

instruction: How do I list top 10 processes consuming the most memory?
output:
Command: ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -n 11
Meaning: Sorts running processes by memory usage percentage descending.

instruction: How do I list top 10 processes consuming the most CPU?
output:
Command: ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head -n 11
Meaning: Sorts running processes by CPU utilization percentage descending.

instruction: How do I find the parent PID (PPID) of a process?
output:
Command: ps -o pid,ppid,comm -p 1234
Meaning: Displays the PID, Parent PID, and executable name for process 1234.

instruction: How do I send a custom signal like SIGUSR1 to a process?
output:
Command: kill -SIGUSR1 1234
Meaning: Sends the user-defined signal SIGUSR1 to process 1234.

instruction: How do I temporarily pause a running process without killing it?
output:
Command: kill -STOP 1234
Meaning: Sends SIGSTOP to freeze execution of the process.

instruction: How do I resume a paused process?
output:
Command: kill -CONT 1234
Meaning: Sends SIGCONT to unfreeze and resume a suspended process.

instruction: How do I monitor disk read and write I/O per process?
output:
Command: sudo iotop
Meaning: Provides a live top-like interface showing disk read/write bandwidth per process.

instruction: How do I see all open files and sockets held by a PID?
output:
Command: ls -l /proc/1234/fd
Meaning: Lists every file descriptor currently opened by process 1234.

instruction: How do I inspect the environment variables of a running process?
output:
Command: cat /proc/1234/environ | tr '\0' '\n'
Meaning: Dumps the environment variables passed to PID 1234 line by line.

instruction: How do I see who owns a running process?
output:
Command: ps -u -p 1234
Meaning: Prints user, CPU, memory, start time, and command name for PID 1234.

instruction: How do I terminate all processes owned by user guest?
output:
Command: sudo pkill -u guest
Meaning: Sends terminate signal to every process owned by user 'guest'.
Warning: Forces all user sessions to close.

instruction: How do I view lightweight threads running within a process?
output:
Command: ps -T -p 1234
Meaning: Lists all threads (SPID/LWP) running inside process 1234.

instruction: How do I view the memory map and shared libraries of a PID?
output:
Command: pmap -x 1234
Meaning: Shows virtual address ranges, RSS, and mapped libraries for PID 1234.

instruction: How do I benchmark the real and CPU execution time of a command?
output:
Command: time ./test_script.sh
Meaning: Measures real elapsed clock time, user CPU time, and kernel system time.

instruction: How do I list process state codes like sleeping or zombie?
output:
Command: ps -eo pid,stat,comm
Meaning: Prints status codes: R (running), S (interruptible sleep), D (disk sleep), Z (zombie).

instruction: How do I filter specifically for zombie processes?
output:
Command: ps aux | grep '[Zz]'
Meaning: Finds terminated child processes awaiting cleanup by their parent.

instruction: How do I throttle a CPU-hogging process to 30% utilization?
output:
Command: cpulimit -p 1234 -l 30
Meaning: Limits the maximum CPU usage of process 1234 to 30%.

instruction: How do I monitor process context switching rates?
output:
Command: pidstat -w 1 3
Meaning: Tracks voluntary and involuntary context switches per second for processes.

instruction: How do I run a status check every 2 seconds automatically?
output:
Command: watch -n 2 'ps aux | wc -l'
Meaning: Executes the command repeatedly every 2 seconds, displaying the output.

instruction: How do I trace system calls of a currently running PID?
output:
Command: sudo strace -p 1234
Meaning: Attaches to PID 1234 and streams system calls in real time.

instruction: How do I view the systemd service managing a process?
output:
Command: systemctl status <PID>
Meaning: Displays the service name, cgroup, memory footprint, and log snippet.

instruction: How do I list files with detailed permissions, size, and date?
output:
Command: ls -l
Meaning: Lists directory contents in long format showing permissions, owner, size, and timestamp.

instruction: How do I list all files including hidden dotfiles?
output:
Command: ls -a
Meaning: Lists every file in the directory including hidden files that begin with a dot.

instruction: How do I display files in human-readable sizes?
output:
Command: ls -lh
Meaning: Lists files in long format with file sizes displayed in K, M, or G units.

instruction: How do I sort files by modification time newest first?
output:
Command: ls -lt
Meaning: Lists files sorted by latest modification timestamp first.

instruction: How do I sort files by size largest first?
output:
Command: ls -lS
Meaning: Sorts directory contents starting with the largest file.

instruction: How do I create a new empty directory?
output:
Command: mkdir my_folder
Meaning: Creates a directory named my_folder in the current working directory.

instruction: How do I create nested parent directories in one command?
output:
Command: mkdir -p project/src/utils
Meaning: Creates parent and child directory trees without throwing errors if they exist.

instruction: How do I copy a single file to another location?
output:
Command: cp source.txt destination.txt
Meaning: Duplicates source.txt to destination.txt.

instruction: How do I copy an entire directory recursively?
output:
Command: cp -r folder1/ folder2/
Meaning: Copies folder1 and all nested files and subdirectories into folder2.

instruction: How do I copy files preserving permissions and timestamps?
output:
Command: cp -a src/ dest/
Meaning: Archive copy that preserves modes, ownership, timestamps, and symlinks.

instruction: How do I move or rename a file?
output:
Command: mv old_name.txt new_name.txt
Meaning: Renames old_name.txt to new_name.txt or moves it if destination is a directory.

instruction: How do I delete a single file permanently?
output:
Command: rm document.pdf
Meaning: Removes the file permanently from the file system.
Warning: Deleted files cannot be restored from a recycle bin.

instruction: How do I prompt for confirmation before deleting files?
output:
Command: rm -i *.log
Meaning: Prompts the user interactively before deleting each matching file.

instruction: How do I recursively delete a folder and all its contents?
output:
Command: rm -rf folder_name
Meaning: Forcefully deletes the directory and everything inside it without confirmation.
Warning: Irreversible operation. Verify path carefully before executing.

instruction: How do I delete an empty directory?
output:
Command: rmdir empty_dir
Meaning: Removes the directory only if it contains no files.

instruction: How do I find files larger than 100MB in the root filesystem?
output:
Command: find / -type f -size +100M
Meaning: Searches the root directory for regular files greater than 100 megabytes.

instruction: How do I search for a file by exact name in current directory?
output:
Command: find . -name 'config.json'
Meaning: Locates files named config.json recursively starting from current directory.

instruction: How do I search for files case-insensitively?
output:
Command: find . -iname '*.png'
Meaning: Finds all files ending in .png, .PNG, or any case variation.

instruction: How do I find all directories only?
output:
Command: find . -type d
Meaning: Searches and filters results to directories only.

instruction: How do I find files modified within the last 24 hours?
output:
Command: find . -type f -mtime -1
Meaning: Finds files whose data was modified within the last day.

instruction: How do I find empty files and directories?
output:
Command: find . -empty
Meaning: Searches for empty files or directories.

instruction: How do I delete all .tmp files in a directory?
output:
Command: find . -type f -name '*.tmp' -delete
Meaning: Finds and deletes all files matching *.tmp.
Warning: Permanently deletes matching files.

instruction: How do I execute a command on every file found by find?
How do I print the absolute path of the current directory?
output:
Command: pwd
Meaning: Prints the full working directory path.

instruction: How do I resolve the physical path avoiding symlinks?
output:
Command: pwd -P
Meaning: Prints physical directory path with all symbolic links resolved.

instruction: How do I change directory to my user home?
output:
Command: cd ~
Meaning: Navigates to the current user's home directory.

instruction: How do I go up one directory level?
output:
Command: cd ..
Meaning: Changes directory to the immediate parent directory.

instruction: How do I switch back to the previous directory?
output:
Command: cd -
Meaning: Returns to the previously visited directory.

instruction: How do I create a new empty file or update timestamp?
output:
Command: touch file.txt
Meaning: Creates file.txt if it does not exist, or updates its access/modification timestamp.

instruction: How do I create a symbolic link (symlink)?
output:
Command: ln -s /path/to/target link_name
Meaning: Creates a symbolic pointer pointing to the target file or directory.

instruction: How do I create a hard link to a file?
output:
Command: ln original.txt hardlink.txt
Meaning: Creates a directory entry pointing to the same filesystem inode.

instruction: How do I see the inode number of a file?
output:
Command: ls -i file.txt
Meaning: Displays the unique inode index number of file.txt.

instruction: How do I identify the MIME type or format of a file?
output:
Command: file document.bin
Meaning: Inspects file magic bytes and reports file type (e.g. ELF, ASCII, PNG).

instruction: How do I view directory structure as a visual tree?
output:
Command: tree -L 2
Meaning: Draws a visual directory tree limited to 2 levels of depth.

instruction: How do I calculate MD5 hash of a file?
output:
Command: md5sum archive.zip
Meaning: Calculates the 128-bit MD5 cryptographic checksum of the file.

instruction: How do I calculate SHA-256 hash of a file?
output:
Command: sha256sum setup.tar.gz
Meaning: Generates the SHA-256 digest to verify file integrity.

instruction: How do I create a tar.gz compressed archive?
output:
Command: tar -czvf backup.tar.gz /path/to/folder
Meaning: Archives and compresses the directory into a gzip tarball.

instruction: How do I extract a tar.gz archive?
output:
Command: tar -xzvf backup.tar.gz
Meaning: Extracts files from a gzip-compressed tar archive.

instruction: How do I list the contents of a tar file without extracting?
output:
Command: tar -tf archive.tar
Meaning: Lists all files packaged inside the archive without writing to disk.

instruction: How do I extract a tar.bz2 archive?
output:
Command: tar -xjvf file.tar.bz2
Meaning: Extracts files from a bzip2-compressed tarball.

instruction: How do I create a zip archive of a directory?
output:
Command: zip -r archive.zip my_folder/
Meaning: Compresses my_folder recursively into archive.zip.

instruction: How do I extract a zip archive?
output:
Command: unzip archive.zip -d dest_dir/
Meaning: Extracts all files from archive.zip into dest_dir/.

instruction: How do I compare two files line by line?
output:
Command: diff -u file1.txt file2.txt
Meaning: Shows differences between two text files in unified diff format.

instruction: How do I compare two directories?
output:
Command: diff -r dir1/ dir2/
Meaning: Recursively compares contents of two directories and flags differences.

instruction: How do I count total files in current folder?
output:
Command: ls -1 | wc -l
Meaning: Lists one entry per line and counts the total number of lines.

instruction: How do I view disk consumption of individual files in a directory?
output:
Command: du -ah --max-depth=1 .
Meaning: Reports sizes of all files and immediate subdirectories in readable format.

instruction: How do I find broken symbolic links?
output:
Command: find . -xtype l
Meaning: Locates symlinks whose target file has been moved or deleted.

instruction: How do I safely wipe a file by overwriting it?
output:
Command: shred -u secret.txt
Meaning: Overwrites the file with random bits before removing it to prevent recovery.
Warning: Irreversibly destroys file contents.

instruction: How do I locate binaries and man pages for a command?
output:
Command: whereis ls
Meaning: Searches standard binary, source, and manual page directories for 'ls'.

instruction: How do I find which exact binary executable runs for a command?
output:
Command: which python3
Meaning: Prints the absolute filesystem path of the executable located in PATH.

instruction: How do I display file metadata and timestamps with stat?
output:
Command: stat document.txt
Meaning: Shows size, blocks, IO block, inode, links, access, modify, and change times.

instruction: How do I sync files between two directories efficiently?
output:
Command: rsync -avh source/ destination/
Meaning: Copies only modified blocks between directories, preserving permissions.

instruction: How do I show progress while copying large files?
output:
Command: rsync -ah --progress file.iso /mnt/backup/
Meaning: Transfers file while displaying a real-time progress bar and transfer speed.

instruction: How do I list hidden files only?
output:
Command: ls -d .*
Meaning: Lists files and directories starting with a dot in current directory.

instruction: How do I find files with specific permissions?
output:
Command: find . -type f -perm 644
Meaning: Searches for files having exact permission bits 644 (rw-r--r--).

instruction: How do I find files owned by a specific user?
output:
Command: find /home -user student
Meaning: Locates all files owned by username student.

instruction: How do I read first 512 bytes of a file?
output:
Command: head -c 512 file.dat
Meaning: Extracts the initial 512 bytes from the file.

instruction: How do I split a large file into 100MB chunks?
output:
Command: split -b 100M large.zip chunk_
Meaning: Splits the file into pieces prefixed with chunk_.

instruction: How do I rejoin split files into one?
output:
Command: cat chunk_* > restored.zip
Meaning: Concatenates all chunk files back into restored.zip.

instruction: How do I create a temporary file securely in bash?
output:
Command: mktemp /tmp/mytemp.XXXXXX
Meaning: Creates a unique, unguessable temporary file in /tmp.

instruction: How do I make a shell script executable?
output:
Command: chmod +x script.sh
Meaning: Adds execute permission to the user, group, and others.

instruction: How do I grant read, write, and execute to owner only?
output:
Command: chmod 700 file.sh
Meaning: Owner gets rwx; group and others have zero permissions.

instruction: How do I give owner full access and others read-only?
output:
Command: chmod 755 script.py
Meaning: Owner gets rwx (7); group and others get r-x (5).

instruction: How do I set standard file permissions to read and write for owner, read for others?
output:
Command: chmod 644 document.txt
Meaning: Standard secure file permission (rw-r--r--).

instruction: How do I make a file read-only for everyone?
output:
Command: chmod 444 config.ini
Meaning: Removes write permission from owner, group, and all users.

instruction: How do I recursively change permissions for a folder and its contents?
output:
Command: chmod -R 755 my_folder/
Meaning: Applies 755 permissions to the folder and every nested file/directory.

instruction: How do I give everyone full read, write, and execute permissions?
output:
Command: chmod 777 folder/
Meaning: Grants total unrestricted read, write, and execute permissions to all users.
Warning: Extremely dangerous. Anyone on the machine can modify or delete files.

instruction: How do I recursively give everyone full access to a folder?
output:
Command: chmod -R 777 shared/
Meaning: Grants everyone rwx permissions across all nested files and folders.
Warning: Severe security vulnerability. Verify carefully.

instruction: How do I change the owner of a file?
output:
Command: sudo chown student file.txt
Meaning: Changes user ownership of file.txt to user 'student'.

instruction: How do I change both owner and group of a file?
output:
Command: sudo chown student:developers file.txt
Meaning: Sets user ownership to student and group to developers.

instruction: How do I recursively change owner of an entire directory?
output:
Command: sudo chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/html
Meaning: Applies new user and group ownership to all files and subfolders.

instruction: How do I change the group ownership only?
output:
Command: chgrp staff document.pdf
Meaning: Sets group ownership of document.pdf to group staff.

instruction: How do I view default file creation permissions (umask)?
output:
Command: umask
Meaning: Prints current umask mask octal (e.g. 0022).

instruction: How do I set umask so new files have no permissions for others?
output:
Command: umask 027
Meaning: New files are created with 640 and directories with 750 permissions.

instruction: How do I set the SUID bit on an executable?
output:
Command: chmod u+s /usr/local/bin/custom_tool
Meaning: Causes executable to run with privileges of the file owner.
Warning: SUID binaries can pose severe security escalation risks.

instruction: How do I set the SGID bit on a directory?
output:
Command: chmod g+s shared_folder/
Meaning: Ensures files created in the folder inherit the group ownership of the directory.

instruction: How do I set the sticky bit on a directory?
output:
Command: chmod +t /tmp/shared_dir
Meaning: Ensures only file owners can delete their own files in the directory (like /tmp).

instruction: How do I remove the sticky bit from a directory?
output:
Command: chmod -t folder/
Meaning: Removes the restricted deletion flag from the directory.

instruction: How do I remove write permission from group and others?
output:
Command: chmod go-w file.txt
Meaning: Revokes write permission for group and others while keeping owner intact.

instruction: How do I add execute permission for owner only?
output:
Command: chmod u+x run.sh
Meaning: Adds execute permission exclusively for the file's owner.

instruction: How do I see extended Access Control Lists (ACL) on a file?
output:
Command: getfacl document.pdf
Meaning: Displays detailed POSIX Access Control Lists for users and groups.

instruction: How do I grant read and write ACL permission to user alex?
output:
Command: setfacl -m u:alex:rw document.pdf
Meaning: Grants user alex rw permissions without modifying primary file owner.

instruction: How do I remove all extended ACL permissions from a file?
output:
Command: setfacl -b document.pdf
Meaning: Strips all extended ACL entries reverting to standard POSIX permissions.

instruction: How do I view file attributes including immutable flag?
output:
Command: lsattr file.txt
Meaning: Displays extended ext4/xfs file attributes.

instruction: How do I make a file immutable so even root cannot delete it?
output:
Command: sudo chattr +i critical.conf
Meaning: Locks the file preventing modification, renaming, or deletion.

instruction: How do I remove the immutable attribute from a file?
output:
Command: sudo chattr -i critical.conf
Meaning: Unlocks the immutable flag allowing the file to be edited or deleted.

instruction: How do I make a file append-only?
output:
Command: sudo chattr +a audit.log
Meaning: Permits only appending new lines to the file, disallowing overwrite.

instruction: How do I copy permissions from one file to another?
output:
Command: chmod --reference=sample.txt target.txt
Meaning: Sets permissions on target.txt to exactly match sample.txt.

instruction: How do I find all SUID executables on the system?
output:
Command: find / -perm -4000 -type f 2>/dev/null
Meaning: Scans filesystem for programs with the SUID bit set.

instruction: How do I find all SGID files on the system?
output:
Command: find / -perm -2000 -type f 2>/dev/null
Meaning: Locates all binaries and directories with the SGID bit enabled.

instruction: How do I find world-writable files on the machine?
output:
Command: find / -perm -o+w -type f 2>/dev/null
Meaning: Identifies files writable by any unprivileged user.

instruction: How do I see which groups current user belongs to?
output:
Command: groups
Meaning: Prints all group memberships of the active user session.

instruction: How do I view current user ID, group ID, and security context?
output:
Command: id
Meaning: Displays UID, GID, and list of supplementary groups.

instruction: How do I switch to superuser root account?
output:
Command: sudo -i
Meaning: Starts an interactive root login shell with root environment.

instruction: How do I run a command as another user?
output:
Command: sudo -u student python app.py
Meaning: Executes the specified command under the privileges of user student.

instruction: How do I check free disk space on mounted filesystems?
output:
Command: df -h
Meaning: Shows total, used, and free disk space in human-readable gigabytes and megabytes.

instruction: How do I display disk space along with filesystem types?
output:
Command: df -hT
Meaning: Shows partition capacity alongside filesystem type (ext4, xfs, btrfs).

instruction: How do I check free disk space for a specific partition?
output:
Command: df -h /
Meaning: Displays free and utilized space exclusively for the root mount point.

instruction: How do I check inode exhaustion on filesystems?
output:
Command: df -i
Meaning: Displays total, used, and available filesystem inodes.

instruction: How do I see the total disk size of the current directory?
output:
Command: du -sh .
Meaning: Calculates and prints the aggregate disk space consumed by current folder.

instruction: How do I sort folders in current directory by size largest first?
output:
Command: du -sh * | sort -h
Meaning: Prints directory sizes sorted in human-readable ascending order.

instruction: How do I check total, used, and available RAM and Swap?
output:
Command: free -h
Meaning: Displays physical RAM and swap space utilization in readable units.

instruction: How do I monitor memory usage continuously every 2 seconds?
output:
Command: free -h -s 2
Meaning: Continuously prints RAM and swap stats every 2 seconds.

instruction: How do I list all block storage devices and partitions?
output:
Command: lsblk
Meaning: Displays block devices, partition layout, and mount points in a tree.

instruction: How do I see block devices with UUIDs and filesystem formats?
output:
Command: lsblk -f
Meaning: Prints device names with UUIDs, labels, and filesystem formats.

instruction: How do I view all disk partitions and sector tables?
output:
Command: sudo fdisk -l
Meaning: Lists all physical drives, partition tables, sectors, and disk identifiers.

instruction: How do I mount a partition to a directory?
output:
Command: sudo mount /dev/sdb1 /mnt/data
Meaning: Attaches partition /dev/sdb1 to the directory /mnt/data.
Warning: Verify device identifier before mounting.

instruction: How do I mount a disk partition read-only?
output:
Command: sudo mount -o ro /dev/sdb1 /mnt/data
Meaning: Mounts filesystem in read-only mode to prevent write modifications.

instruction: How do I unmount a filesystem safely?
output:
Command: sudo umount /mnt/data
Meaning: Detaches the mounted filesystem and flushes dirty write caches.

instruction: How do I force unmount an unresponsive network share?
output:
Command: sudo umount -f -l /mnt/share
Meaning: Forces lazy unmount detaching the filesystem immediately.

instruction: How do I format a partition to ext4 filesystem?
output:
Command: sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdb1
Meaning: Creates a fresh ext4 filesystem on partition /dev/sdb1.
Warning: Destroys all existing data on the partition.

instruction: How do I format a partition to XFS filesystem?
output:
Command: sudo mkfs.xfs -f /dev/sdb1
Meaning: Formats partition /dev/sdb1 with an XFS filesystem.
Warning: Overwrites all existing files on the device.

instruction: How do I format a flash drive to FAT32 for universal compatibility?
output:
Command: sudo mkfs.vfat -F 32 /dev/sdb1
Meaning: Creates a FAT32 filesystem compatible with Windows and Linux.
Warning: All partition data is permanently deleted.

instruction: How do I check and repair an unmounted ext4 filesystem?
output:
Command: sudo fsck -f /dev/sdb1
Meaning: Scans partition for filesystem errors and repairs corrupt inodes.
Warning: Must be run on an unmounted filesystem.

instruction: How do I check hardware health and SMART status of a drive?
output:
Command: sudo smartctl -H /dev/sda
Meaning: Reads SMART diagnostic telemetry to check drive reliability.

instruction: How do I benchmark disk read speed?
